title: Systems View
summary: Repeating task = Trigger → Process → Output — the virtual worker needs the map.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Any repeated task = system: Trigger → Process → Output. When you see it this way, you can hand it over to the virtual worker.
- Why now? After identifying which tasks consume your time, the next step is to break one of them down into clear parts.
- What after the lesson? You will convert one repeated task into a Trigger + Process + Output.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- "Reply to this message" — every day from the start: new message → think → search → respond → forget to log it.
- Think of separate tasks — not as a system. The result: the same work repeats, and nothing accumulates.
- The virtual worker needs a map — not a random task list.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: Trigger → Process → Output
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Trigger: What starts the work? — WhatsApp message, new form, scheduled appointment.
- Process: What steps do you take each time? — Understand the request, search for the price, make a decision.
- Output: What comes out in the end? — Response to the client, entry in a table, reminder.
- Example: "Respond to a WhatsApp inquiry" = Trigger: Message → Process: Understanding + Price Search → Output: Response + Log.
- When you break down the task this way, the virtual worker knows exactly where to work.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Separate Task vs Clear System
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Task Thinking | System Thinking |
|----------------|----------------|
| "I need to reply to the message" — every time from the start, with no fixed steps. Hard to hand over to someone or a tool. | "Inquiry Response System": Trigger = Message → Process = 4 fixed steps → Output = Response + CRM. Can be improved or automated. |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Terms for the System
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|--------|
| Trigger | The event that starts the system — without it, nothing moves | A client sends "How much?" on WhatsApp |
| Output | What comes out of the system when finished — what the virtual worker "delivers" | Response with the price + new entry in the client table |

sections.heading: Screenshot Block
sections.contentMarkdown: Connected layers — each layer has an input, processing, and output. Any repeated work = layers stacked: something enters → steps transform → something exits. The same idea applies to a task from your work — it doesn't need to be complicated.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: A client sends a message on Facebook asking about the price of a product. In the "Response System," what is the Trigger?
The new client message
Explanation: Trigger = the event that starts the system. Here, it is the client message — not the price list or CRM entry (those are the process and output).

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Break Down a Repeated Task into a System
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Choose one task you do every week (from Time Inventory). Break it down into Trigger + Process + Output — this is design, not tool building. 10–15 minutes is enough. Submission: Task name · Trigger (what starts it, when/from whom) · Process (at least 4 steps in order) · Output (what comes out and for whom) · If you will automate only one step — which one and why? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| System Breakdown | 70% | A specific and repeated task from your work; Trigger + 4 process steps + clear output |
| Automation Step | 30% | You chose one step because of (repetition / time / errors) |
